gloss: Tomorrow I am taking the bus.
sentence: F:i morgen | v:tager | n:jeg | N:bussen
alternatives: F:jeg | v:tager | N:bussen | A:i morgen
takeaway: Start with "i morgen" and "jeg" has to wait until after the verb "tager".

gloss: In the evening we watch TV.
sentence: F:om aftenen | v:ser | n:vi | N:tv
alternatives: F:vi | v:ser | N:tv | A:om aftenen
takeaway: The verb stays second, so with "om aftenen" in front, "vi" comes after "ser".

gloss: At the weekend we visit my mother.
sentence: F:i weekenden | v:besøger | n:vi | N:min mor
alternatives: F:vi | v:besøger | N:min mor | A:i weekenden
takeaway: A time phrase in front pushes the subject behind the verb: "besøger vi", not "vi besøger".

gloss: School starts at eight o'clock.
sentence: F:klokken otte | v:begynder | n:skolen
alternatives: F:skolen | v:begynder | A:klokken otte
takeaway: The subject does not have to come first. "Klokken otte" can open the sentence, and then "skolen" follows the verb.

gloss: My brother lives in Aarhus.
sentence: F:i Aarhus | v:bor | n:min bror
alternatives: F:min bror | v:bor | A:i Aarhus
takeaway: You can put a place first too. Then the verb comes next and the subject after it.

gloss: After school the children play football.
sentence: F:efter skolen | v:spiller | n:børnene | N:fodbold
alternatives: F:børnene | v:spiller | N:fodbold | A:efter skolen
takeaway: "Efter skolen" takes the front slot, so "børnene" has to follow "spiller".

gloss: On Sundays I sleep late.
sentence: F:om søndagen | v:sover | n:jeg | A:længe
alternatives: F:jeg | v:sover | A:længe | A:om søndagen
takeaway: Same pattern every time: one thing in front, then the verb, then the subject.

gloss: This summer we are travelling to Spain.
sentence: F:i sommer | v:rejser | n:vi | A:til Spanien
alternatives: F:vi | v:rejser | A:til Spanien | A:i sommer
F:til Spanien | v:rejser | n:vi | A:i sommer
takeaway: With "i sommer" in front, the verb "rejser" keeps slot 2 and "vi" moves behind it.

gloss: Every day I cycle to work.
sentence: F:hver dag | v:cykler | n:jeg | A:på arbejde
alternatives: F:jeg | v:cykler | A:på arbejde | A:hver dag
takeaway: "Hver dag" is one constituent in the front slot, and "jeg" follows the verb.

gloss: I live in Odense.
sentence: F:jeg | v:bor | A:i Odense
alternatives: F:i Odense | v:bor | n:jeg
takeaway: Subject first, verb second: the most basic Danish sentence.

gloss: We eat dinner at six o'clock.
sentence: F:vi | v:spiser | N:aftensmad | A:klokken seks
alternatives: F:klokken seks | v:spiser | n:vi | N:aftensmad
takeaway: The verb "spiser" is in slot 2, the object comes next and the time comes last.

gloss: My daughter goes to school.
sentence: F:min datter | v:går | A:i skole
takeaway: "Min datter" is one constituent, even though it is two words, so "går" is still the second constituent.

gloss: He drinks coffee every morning.
sentence: F:han | v:drikker | N:kaffe | A:hver morgen
alternatives: F:hver morgen | v:drikker | n:han | N:kaffe
takeaway: The finite verb "drikker" holds slot 2. Move "hver morgen" to the front and it still does.

gloss: The bus comes at ten o'clock.
sentence: F:bussen | v:kommer | A:klokken ti
alternatives: F:klokken ti | v:kommer | n:bussen
takeaway: One constituent before the verb, here the subject "bussen", and then the verb.

gloss: I speak a little Danish.
sentence: F:jeg | v:taler | N:lidt dansk
takeaway: Subject, verb, object: the verb is second, as in every main clause.

gloss: Peter works at a hospital.
sentence: F:Peter | v:arbejder | A:på et hospital
alternatives: F:på et hospital | v:arbejder | n:Peter
takeaway: The name is the subject and fills the front slot. The verb follows directly.

gloss: We shop at Netto on Saturdays.
sentence: F:vi | v:handler | A:i Netto | A:om lørdagen
alternatives: F:i Netto | v:handler | n:vi | A:om lørdagen
F:om lørdagen | v:handler | n:vi | A:i Netto
takeaway: Place before time at the end of the sentence. If you start with "om lørdagen", the subject moves behind the verb.

gloss: The children are playing in the garden.
sentence: F:børnene | v:leger | A:i haven
alternatives: F:i haven | v:leger | n:børnene
takeaway: The verb takes slot 2 no matter how long the subject is.

gloss: My husband is cooking today.
sentence: F:min mand | v:laver | N:mad | A:i dag
alternatives: F:i dag | v:laver | n:min mand | N:mad
takeaway: "Laver" is the finite verb and is second. "Mad" is the object, and "i dag" comes last.

gloss: She reads a book in bed.
sentence: F:hun | v:læser | N:en bog | A:i sengen
alternatives: F:i sengen | v:læser | n:hun | N:en bog
takeaway: Subject, verb, object, place: the plain order for a main clause.

gloss: Every Sunday I visit my grandmother.
sentence: F:hver søndag | v:besøger | n:jeg | N:min mormor
alternatives: F:jeg | v:besøger | N:min mormor | A:hver søndag
takeaway: "Hver søndag" counts as one constituent. Only it may stand before the verb, so "jeg" comes after.

gloss: Next week my new job starts.
sentence: F:i næste uge | v:starter | n:mit nye job
alternatives: F:mit nye job | v:starter | A:i næste uge
takeaway: Two constituents ("i næste uge" and "mit nye job") cannot both stand before the verb.

gloss: In the morning my wife takes the train.
sentence: F:om morgenen | v:tager | n:min kone | N:toget
alternatives: F:min kone | v:tager | N:toget | A:om morgenen
takeaway: Never "Om morgenen min kone tager…". The front slot has room for one constituent only.

gloss: Last year we moved to Denmark.
sentence: F:sidste år | v:flyttede | n:vi | A:til Danmark
alternatives: F:vi | v:flyttede | A:til Danmark | A:sidste år
F:til Danmark | v:flyttede | n:vi | A:sidste år
takeaway: "Sidste år" fills the front slot alone, so the verb "flyttede" comes before "vi".

gloss: After lunch we go for a walk.
sentence: F:efter frokost | v:går | n:vi | N:en tur
alternatives: F:vi | v:går | N:en tur | A:efter frokost
takeaway: One constituent in front, the verb second, then the subject.

gloss: It rained all weekend.
sentence: F:hele weekenden | v:regnede | n:det
alternatives: F:det | v:regnede | A:hele weekenden
takeaway: "Hele weekenden" takes the front slot, and the dummy subject "det" still has to appear after the verb.

gloss: Every single day I learn new words.
sentence: F:hver eneste dag | v:lærer | n:jeg | N:nye ord
alternatives: F:jeg | v:lærer | N:nye ord | A:hver eneste dag
takeaway: A long time phrase is still a single constituent: "hver eneste dag" plus the verb, then "jeg".

gloss: In my class everyone speaks English.
sentence: F:i min klasse | v:taler | n:alle | N:engelsk
alternatives: F:alle | v:taler | N:engelsk | A:i min klasse
takeaway: "I min klasse" is the only constituent before the verb, and "alle" comes after it.

gloss: In two weeks we are going on holiday.
sentence: F:om to uger | v:holder | n:vi | N:ferie
alternatives: F:vi | v:holder | N:ferie | A:om to uger
takeaway: "Om to uger" is one unit in the front slot, and "vi" moves behind "holder".

gloss: It is snowing today.
sentence: F:det | v:sner | A:i dag
alternatives: F:i dag | v:sner | n:det
takeaway: Danish has no sentence without a subject. Weather verbs use "det".

gloss: It is very windy.
sentence: F:det | v:blæser | A:meget
takeaway: "Blæser meget" is not a sentence on its own. The empty subject "det" has to be there.

gloss: There is a man standing outside.
sentence: F:der | v:står | n:en mand | A:udenfor
alternatives: F:der | v:står | N:en mand | A:udenfor
F:udenfor | v:står | n:der | N:en mand
takeaway: "Der" holds the subject position, so the real subject "en mand" can come after the verb.

gloss: There is a letter on the table.
sentence: F:der | v:ligger | n:et brev | A:på bordet
alternatives: F:der | v:ligger | N:et brev | A:på bordet
F:på bordet | v:ligger | n:der | N:et brev
takeaway: To say that something is somewhere, use "der": "Der ligger et brev…".

gloss: It rained all day.
sentence: F:det | v:regnede | A:hele dagen
alternatives: F:hele dagen | v:regnede | n:det
takeaway: Even when nobody is doing anything, the verb needs a subject: "det".

gloss: There are many students living in Aarhus.
sentence: F:der | v:bor | n:mange studerende | A:i Aarhus
alternatives: F:der | v:bor | N:mange studerende | A:i Aarhus
F:i Aarhus | v:bor | n:der | N:mange studerende
takeaway: New information follows the verb, and "der" fills the subject position at the start.

gloss: There is a shop on the corner.
sentence: F:der | v:er | n:en butik | A:på hjørnet
alternatives: F:der | v:er | N:en butik | A:på hjørnet
F:på hjørnet | v:er | n:der | N:en butik
takeaway: "Der er" means "there is". Without "der" the sentence has no subject.

gloss: It smells good in the kitchen.
sentence: F:det | v:lugter | A:godt | A:i køkkenet
alternatives: F:i køkkenet | v:lugter | n:det | A:godt
takeaway: "Det" is a dummy subject here. It refers to nothing, but Danish still needs it.

gloss: We are out of milk in the fridge.
sentence: F:der | v:mangler | n:mælk | A:i køleskabet
alternatives: F:der | v:mangler | N:mælk | A:i køleskabet
F:i køleskabet | v:mangler | n:der | N:mælk
takeaway: "Der mangler" introduces something that is missing, and "der" is the subject.

gloss: I never eat meat.
sentence: F:jeg | v:spiser | a:aldrig | N:kød
takeaway: "Aldrig" comes straight after the verb, before the object "kød".

gloss: She does not drink coffee.
sentence: F:hun | v:drikker | a:ikke | N:kaffe
takeaway: Danish has no "do". "Ikke" goes directly after the finite verb.

gloss: We also work at weekends.
sentence: F:vi | v:arbejder | a:også | A:i weekenden
alternatives: F:i weekenden | v:arbejder | n:vi | a:også
takeaway: "Også" is a sentence adverb and sits right after the verb. The time phrase "i weekenden" comes at the end.

gloss: He always comes too late.
sentence: F:han | v:kommer | a:altid | A:for sent
takeaway: "Altid" goes early, after the verb. "For sent" is a content adverbial and goes at the end.

gloss: On Monday I have to go to the doctor.
sentence: F:på mandag | v:skal | n:jeg | A:til lægen
alternatives: F:jeg | v:skal | A:til lægen | A:på mandag
F:til lægen | v:skal | n:jeg | A:på mandag
takeaway: The time phrase goes in front, the verb "skal" keeps slot 2 and "jeg" follows it.

gloss: That is why I am staying at home today.
sentence: F:derfor | v:bliver | n:jeg | A:hjemme | A:i dag
alternatives: F:jeg | v:bliver | a:derfor | A:hjemme | A:i dag
F:i dag | v:bliver | n:jeg | a:derfor | A:hjemme
takeaway: "Derfor" in front causes inversion just like a time phrase does: "derfor bliver jeg", never "derfor jeg bliver".

gloss: This evening we have a parents' meeting.
sentence: F:i aften | v:har | n:vi | N:et forældremøde
alternatives: F:vi | v:har | N:et forældremøde | A:i aften
takeaway: Front "i aften" and the subject "vi" moves to the other side of the verb.

gloss: In winter I do not cycle to work.
sentence: F:om vinteren | v:cykler | n:jeg | a:ikke | A:på arbejde
alternatives: F:jeg | v:cykler | a:ikke | A:på arbejde | A:om vinteren
takeaway: After inversion the order is verb, subject, "ikke": "cykler jeg ikke".

gloss: Fortunately my sister got a job last month.
sentence: F:heldigvis | v:fik | n:min søster | N:et job | A:i sidste måned
alternatives: F:min søster | v:fik | a:heldigvis | N:et job | A:i sidste måned
F:i sidste måned | v:fik | n:min søster | a:heldigvis | N:et job
takeaway: "Heldigvis" can open the sentence, and then the verb comes next: "heldigvis fik min søster".

gloss: Perhaps we will move to Odense next year.
sentence: F:måske | v:flytter | n:vi | A:til Odense | A:næste år
alternatives: F:vi | v:flytter | a:måske | A:til Odense | A:næste år
F:til Odense | v:flytter | n:vi | a:måske | A:næste år
F:næste år | v:flytter | n:vi | a:måske | A:til Odense
takeaway: "Måske" in front behaves like any other fronted element. The verb comes second, then the subject.

gloss: Our neighbours have a party every Friday.
sentence: F:vores naboer | v:holder | N:fest | A:hver fredag
alternatives: F:hver fredag | v:holder | n:vores naboer | N:fest
takeaway: "Vores naboer" is one constituent, and "holder" is second.

gloss: The Danish course starts in August.
sentence: F:danskkurset | v:starter | A:i august
alternatives: F:i august | v:starter | n:danskkurset
takeaway: One constituent, then the finite verb. That is the whole V2 rule.

gloss: My new colleague comes from Poland.
sentence: F:min nye kollega | v:kommer | A:fra Polen
alternatives: F:fra Polen | v:kommer | n:min nye kollega
takeaway: However long the subject is, the verb follows straight after it.

gloss: We are moving next month.
sentence: F:vi | v:skal | V:flytte | A:i næste måned
alternatives: F:i næste måned | v:skal | n:vi | V:flytte
takeaway: Only the finite verb "skal" is second. The infinitive "flytte" waits further back.

gloss: The trains are not running today.
sentence: F:togene | v:kører | a:ikke | A:i dag
alternatives: F:i dag | v:kører | n:togene | a:ikke
takeaway: "Kører" is second and "ikke" follows it, as in every main clause.

gloss: The doctor will call tomorrow morning.
sentence: F:lægen | v:ringer | A:i morgen formiddag
alternatives: F:i morgen formiddag | v:ringer | n:lægen
takeaway: Danish often uses the present tense for the future, and the verb is still second.

gloss: At my workplace we have a big canteen.
sentence: F:på mit arbejde | v:har | n:vi | N:en stor kantine
alternatives: F:vi | v:har | N:en stor kantine | A:på mit arbejde
takeaway: "På mit arbejde" is three words but one constituent. It fills the front slot alone.

gloss: After the Danish course I would like to find a job.
sentence: F:efter danskkurset | v:vil | n:jeg | a:gerne | V:finde | N:et job
alternatives: F:jeg | v:vil | a:gerne | V:finde | N:et job | A:efter danskkurset
takeaway: Never "Efter danskkurset jeg vil…". With one constituent in front, "vil" has to come next.

gloss: In my free time I play the guitar.
sentence: F:i min fritid | v:spiller | n:jeg | N:guitar
alternatives: F:jeg | v:spiller | N:guitar | A:i min fritid
takeaway: "I min fritid" is one constituent in the front slot, so "jeg" comes after "spiller".

gloss: Every other week I have my children.
sentence: F:hver anden uge | v:har | n:jeg | N:mine børn
alternatives: F:jeg | v:har | N:mine børn | A:hver anden uge
takeaway: "Hver anden uge" is a single time constituent. One unit in front, then the verb.

gloss: By train the journey takes two hours.
sentence: F:med toget | v:tager | n:turen | N:to timer
alternatives: F:turen | v:tager | N:to timer | A:med toget
F:turen | v:tager | a:med toget | N:to timer
takeaway: A prepositional phrase in front counts as one constituent and triggers inversion.

gloss: In the spring my son starts kindergarten.
sentence: F:i foråret | v:begynder | n:min søn | A:i børnehave
alternatives: F:min søn | v:begynder | A:i børnehave | A:i foråret
takeaway: "I foråret" stands alone before the verb, and "min søn" comes after it.

gloss: There is no room in the car.
sentence: F:der | v:er | a:ikke | N:plads | A:i bilen
alternatives: F:i bilen | v:er | n:der | a:ikke | N:plads
takeaway: "Der" is the subject. The real subject "plads" comes later, after "ikke".

gloss: It has snowed all night.
sentence: F:det | v:har | V:sneet | A:hele natten
alternatives: F:hele natten | v:har | n:det | V:sneet
takeaway: The weather verb in the perfect still needs "det": "det har sneet".

gloss: There is a cat sitting on the stairs.
sentence: F:der | v:sidder | n:en kat | A:på trappen
alternatives: F:der | v:sidder | N:en kat | A:på trappen
F:på trappen | v:sidder | n:der | N:en kat
takeaway: When the subject is new information, Danish starts with "der" and puts the real subject after the verb.

gloss: Guests are coming this evening.
sentence: F:der | v:kommer | n:gæster | A:i aften
alternatives: F:der | v:kommer | N:gæster | A:i aften
F:i aften | v:kommer | n:der | N:gæster
takeaway: "Kommer gæster i aften" has no subject. "Der" fills that position.

gloss: It has rained a lot this week.
sentence: F:det | v:har | V:regnet | A:meget | A:i denne uge
alternatives: F:i denne uge | v:har | n:det | V:regnet | A:meget
takeaway: "Det" is the subject of the weather verb, even in a verb cluster.

gloss: There is a shortage of educators in many kindergartens.
sentence: F:der | v:mangler | n:pædagoger | A:i mange børnehaver
alternatives: F:der | v:mangler | N:pædagoger | A:i mange børnehaver
F:i mange børnehaver | v:mangler | n:der | N:pædagoger
takeaway: "Der mangler…" is a fixed pattern: "der" is the subject, and the people who are missing come after the verb.

gloss: My son cannot swim.
sentence: F:min søn | v:kan | a:ikke | V:svømme
takeaway: "Kan" is the finite verb and "svømme" the infinitive. "Ikke" goes between them.

gloss: I would like a cup of coffee.
sentence: F:jeg | v:vil | a:gerne | V:have | N:en kop kaffe
takeaway: "Vil gerne have" is split up: "vil" in slot 2, "gerne" in the adverb slot, "have" in V.

gloss: We have lived in Denmark for three years.
sentence: F:vi | v:har | V:boet | A:i Danmark | A:i tre år
alternatives: F:i Danmark | v:har | n:vi | V:boet | A:i tre år
F:i tre år | v:har | n:vi | V:boet | A:i Danmark
takeaway: "Har" is finite and "boet" is the participle. The place comes before the time at the end.

gloss: I have to work on Saturday.
sentence: F:jeg | v:skal | V:arbejde | A:på lørdag
alternatives: F:på lørdag | v:skal | n:jeg | V:arbejde
takeaway: Modal first, infinitive later: "skal … arbejde".

gloss: I have not seen the film.
sentence: F:jeg | v:har | a:ikke | V:set | N:filmen
takeaway: "Har set" is not one block. "Ikke" sits between "har" and "set".

gloss: You may not smoke here.
sentence: F:man | v:må | a:ikke | V:ryge | A:her
alternatives: F:her | v:må | n:man | a:ikke | V:ryge
takeaway: "Må" is finite, so it is second. "Ryge" waits in V after "ikke".

gloss: …because I am not feeling well.
sentence: k:fordi | n:jeg | a:ikke | v:har | N:det | A:godt
takeaway: After "fordi", "ikke" comes before the finite verb: "fordi jeg ikke har".

gloss: …if you cannot come.
sentence: k:hvis | n:du | a:ikke | v:kan | V:komme
takeaway: In a "hvis" clause, "ikke" goes in front of "kan", not after it.

gloss: …that he never smokes.
sentence: k:at | n:han | a:aldrig | v:ryger
takeaway: "At" starts a subordinate clause, so "aldrig" moves in front of the verb.

gloss: …when the bus does not come.
sentence: k:når | n:bussen | a:ikke | v:kommer
takeaway: "Når" works like "fordi" and "hvis": subject, "ikke", then the verb.

gloss: …whether she is also coming this evening.
sentence: k:om | n:hun | a:også | v:kommer | A:i aften
takeaway: The rule covers all sentence adverbs, so "også" also goes before the verb in a subordinate clause.

gloss: …because we do not have a car.
sentence: k:fordi | n:vi | a:ikke | v:har | N:bil
takeaway: Main clause: "Vi har ikke bil." Subordinate clause: "fordi vi ikke har bil."

gloss: …that I bought yesterday.
sentence: k:som | n:jeg | v:købte | A:i går
takeaway: "Som" opens the clause. After it comes the normal subordinate-clause order: subject, verb, time.

gloss: …where my sister lives.
sentence: k:hvor | n:min søster | v:bor
takeaway: "Hvor" can open a relative clause about a place. The subject comes right after it.

gloss: …that she does not like.
sentence: k:som | n:hun | a:ikke | v:kan | V:lide
takeaway: A relative clause is a subordinate clause, so "ikke" goes before "kan".

gloss: …that my mother always makes for Christmas.
sentence: k:som | n:min mor | a:altid | v:laver | A:til jul
takeaway: "Altid" comes before the verb "laver", because "som" made this a subordinate clause.

gloss: …where I worked last year.
sentence: k:hvor | n:jeg | v:arbejdede | A:sidste år
takeaway: After "hvor" comes subject, then verb, then time, with no inversion.

gloss: I gave my wife flowers yesterday.
sentence: F:jeg | v:gav | N:min kone | N:blomster | A:i går
alternatives: F:i går | v:gav | n:jeg | N:min kone | N:blomster
takeaway: The receiver ("min kone") comes before the thing given ("blomster").

gloss: I will show you the way.
sentence: F:jeg | v:viser | N:dig | N:vejen
takeaway: Person first, thing second: "dig vejen", not "vejen dig".

gloss: My neighbour is lending me his bicycle.
sentence: F:min nabo | v:låner | N:mig | N:sin cykel
takeaway: The receiver "mig" comes before what is lent, "sin cykel".

gloss: We are buying the children an ice cream.
sentence: F:vi | v:køber | N:børnene | N:en is
takeaway: With two objects, the person who gets something comes first.

gloss: I will send you a text this evening.
sentence: F:jeg | v:sender | N:dig | N:en sms | A:i aften
alternatives: F:i aften | v:sender | n:jeg | N:dig | N:en sms
takeaway: "Dig" (the receiver) comes before "en sms", and the time comes last.

gloss: My husband is not at home today.
sentence: F:min mand | v:er | a:ikke | A:hjemme | A:i dag
alternatives: F:i dag | v:er | n:min mand | a:ikke | A:hjemme
takeaway: "Ikke" is a sentence adverb and comes early. "Hjemme" and "i dag" are content adverbials and come late.

gloss: We like to eat together in the evening.
sentence: F:vi | v:spiser | a:gerne | A:sammen | A:om aftenen
alternatives: F:om aftenen | v:spiser | n:vi | a:gerne | A:sammen
takeaway: "Gerne" comments on the whole sentence and sits after the verb. "Sammen" and "om aftenen" go at the end.

gloss: He always cycles home fast.
sentence: F:han | v:cykler | a:altid | A:hurtigt | A:hjem
takeaway: "Altid" goes in the adverb slot after the verb. "Hurtigt" (how) and "hjem" (where) go at the end.

gloss: My brother still lives in Aarhus.

F:om natten | v:kører | n:hun | A:forsigtigt | A:i byen

F:af mine forældre | v:fik | n:jeg | N:en cykel | A:til min fødselsdag

gloss: I would like help with my application.

gloss: The parcel was supposed to be delivered yesterday.

takeaway: "Skal være modtaget": one finite verb, two non-finite ones in V.

gloss: I would have liked to take part in the course.

alternatives: F:i kurset | v:ville | n:jeg | a:gerne | V:have | V:deltaget

gloss: The washing machine has still not been repaired.

takeaway: "Stadig ikke" goes between "er" and "blevet repareret", never after the participles.

gloss: …even though I have never worked in Denmark before.
sentence: k:selvom | n:jeg | a:aldrig | v:har | V:arbejdet | A:i Danmark | A:før
takeaway: After "selvom", "aldrig" goes in front of "har". Place and time come last.

gloss: …because my son can no longer attend the local school.
sentence: k:fordi | n:min søn | a:ikke | a:længere | v:kan | V:gå | A:i den lokale skole
takeaway: "Ikke længere" are two sentence adverbs, and both go before "kan".

gloss: …if the flat still has not been renovated.
sentence: k:hvis | n:lejligheden | a:stadig | a:ikke | v:er | V:blevet | V:istandsat
takeaway: "Stadig ikke" goes before the finite verb "er" in a subordinate clause.

gloss: …that unfortunately we cannot offer you an interview.
sentence: k:at | n:vi | a:desværre | a:ikke | v:kan | V:tilbyde | N:Dem | N:en samtale
takeaway: A typical rejection letter: "at vi desværre ikke kan…". Both adverbs go before the verb.

gloss: …whether there is also an option to work part-time.
sentence: k:om | n:der | a:også | v:er | N:mulighed for deltid
takeaway: "Der" is the subject here too, and "også" goes before "er".

gloss: …as I have not received my pay for March.
sentence: k:da | n:jeg | a:ikke | v:har | V:modtaget | N:min løn for marts
takeaway: A "da" clause works like "fordi": "ikke" goes before "har".

gloss: …when you do not speak Danish at the workplace.
sentence: k:når | n:man | a:ikke | v:taler | N:dansk | A:på arbejdspladsen
takeaway: The general "man" is a normal subject, and "ikke" still goes before the verb.

gloss: …that I have not been able to find on the website.
sentence: k:som | n:jeg | a:ikke | v:har | V:kunnet | V:finde | A:på hjemmesiden
takeaway: "Ikke" goes before "har" in the relative clause. "Kunnet finde" waits in V.

gloss: …that my employer has not yet paid out.
sentence: k:som | n:min arbejdsgiver | a:endnu | a:ikke | v:har | V:udbetalt
takeaway: Subject, "endnu ikke", then the finite verb. The schema is the same as after "fordi".

gloss: …where many of the residents do not speak Danish.
sentence: k:hvor | n:mange af beboerne | a:ikke | v:taler | N:dansk
takeaway: "Mange af beboerne" is one subject constituent, and "ikke" follows it before the verb.

gloss: …that the municipality has sent me.
sentence: k:som | n:kommunen | v:har | V:sendt | N:mig
takeaway: "Som" stands for the thing sent, so only "mig" remains as an object.

gloss: …that you can usually get from the doctor.
sentence: k:som | n:man | a:som regel | v:kan | V:få | A:hos lægen
takeaway: "Som regel" is a sentence adverbial and goes before "kan" in the relative clause.

gloss: …where I did my work placement last spring.
sentence: k:hvor | n:jeg | v:havde | N:praktik | A:sidste forår
takeaway: Plain subordinate-clause order after "hvor": subject, verb, object, time.

gloss: …that most Danes know from school.
sentence: k:som | n:de fleste danskere | v:kender | A:fra skolen
takeaway: "De fleste danskere" is the subject and comes right after "som".

gloss: My employer has given me a warning.
sentence: F:min arbejdsgiver | v:har | V:givet | N:mig | N:en advarsel
takeaway: The person receiving it, "mig", comes before what is given, "en advarsel".

gloss: The bank has granted us a loan for a new car.
sentence: F:banken | v:har | V:bevilget | N:os | N:et lån til en ny bil
takeaway: "Bevilge" takes two objects: "os" (receiver) before "et lån…" (thing).

gloss: I sent my caseworker all the papers last week.
sentence: F:jeg | v:sendte | N:min sagsbehandler | N:alle papirerne | A:i sidste uge
alternatives: F:i sidste uge | v:sendte | n:jeg | N:min sagsbehandler | N:alle papirerne
takeaway: "Min sagsbehandler" receives and "alle papirerne" are sent, so the receiver comes first.

gloss: She has promised her children a trip to Legoland.
sentence: F:hun | v:har | V:lovet | N:sine børn | N:en tur til Legoland
takeaway: "Love" works like "give": the person promised comes before the promise.

gloss: The municipality will give all newcomers an introduction programme.
sentence: F:kommunen | v:vil | V:give | N:alle nyankomne | N:et introduktionsforløb

gloss: On Monday I am going to show the new colleagues around the workplace.
sentence: F:jeg | v:skal | V:vise | N:de nye kolleger | N:arbejdspladsen | A:på mandag
alternatives: F:på mandag | v:skal | n:jeg | V:vise | N:de nye kolleger | N:arbejdspladsen

gloss: The pharmacy sold me the wrong medicine.
sentence: F:apoteket | v:solgte | N:mig | N:den forkerte medicin
takeaway: The buyer "mig" comes before the thing sold, "den forkerte medicin".

gloss: Unfortunately the rent has gone up sharply this year.
sentence: F:huslejen | v:er | a:desværre | V:steget | A:kraftigt | A:i år

F:desværre | v:er | n:huslejen | V:steget | A:kraftigt | A:i år
takeaway: "Desværre" is a sentence adverb and comes early. "Kraftigt" and "i år" are content adverbials and come last.

gloss: I probably cannot start before the first of August.

F:sandsynligvis | v:kan | n:jeg | a:ikke | V:starte | A:før den første august

gloss: My husband also works nights at a factory.

F:om natten | v:arbejder | n:min mand | a:også | A:på en fabrik

F:egentlig | v:vil | n:jeg | a:hellere | V:arbejde | A:om dagen

F:hele sommeren | v:har | n:hun | V:arbejdet | A:ulønnet | A:i en butik

F:vi | v:skal | a:i forbindelse med renoveringen | V:flytte | A:midlertidigt | A:til en anden lejlighed
F:til en anden lejlighed | v:skal | n:vi | a:i forbindelse med renoveringen | V:flytte | A:midlertidigt

F:jeg | v:vil | a:på den baggrund | a:gerne | V:klage | A:over den lange sagsbehandlingstid

F:jeg | v:ønsker | a:på baggrund af ovenstående | N:aktindsigt i min sag

gloss: Over the past five years the number of electric cars has risen sharply.

F:i mange år | v:har | n:der | V:været | N:mangel på billige boliger | A:i de store byer

gloss: Unfortunately there are still many lonely elderly people in Denmark.

alternatives: F:i Danmark | v:findes | n:der | a:desværre | a:stadig | N:mange ensomme ældre
F:desværre | v:findes | n:der | a:stadig | N:mange ensomme ældre | A:i Danmark

gloss: The case should have been decided several months ago.

F:i flere dage | v:må | n:brevet | V:have | V:ligget | A:i postkassen

takeaway: "Har ikke kunnet arbejde": "ikke" sits between the finite verb and the non-finite verbs.

gloss: The politicians should have given the state school much higher priority.
sentence: F:politikerne | v:burde | V:have | V:prioriteret | N:folkeskolen | A:langt højere
takeaway: A typical criticism in an opinion text: "burde have" + participle. The finite verb is second.

gloss: The flat will be inspected by a tradesman next week.
sentence: F:lejligheden | v:vil | V:blive | V:gennemgået | A:af en håndværker | A:i næste uge
alternatives: F:i næste uge | v:vil | n:lejligheden | V:blive | V:gennemgået | A:af en håndværker
takeaway: Passive future: "vil" is finite, "blive gennemgået" is in V, and the time comes last.

gloss: I would never have applied for the job without your encouragement.
sentence: F:jeg | v:ville | a:aldrig | V:have | V:søgt | N:stillingen | A:uden din opfordring
alternatives: F:uden din opfordring | v:ville | n:jeg | a:aldrig | V:have | V:søgt | N:stillingen
F:jeg | v:ville | a:uden din opfordring | a:aldrig | V:have | V:søgt | N:stillingen
takeaway: "Ville aldrig have søgt": "aldrig" goes between "ville" and "have søgt".

gloss: …even though I have not yet received a decision in my case.
sentence: k:selvom | n:jeg | a:endnu | a:ikke | v:har | V:modtaget | N:en afgørelse i min sag
takeaway: In a "selvom" clause, "endnu ikke" goes before "har". This is the most common PD3 word-order error.

gloss: …since the housing association has not met its obligations.
sentence: k:eftersom | n:boligselskabet | a:ikke | v:har | V:overholdt | N:sine forpligtelser
takeaway: "Eftersom" starts a subordinate clause, so "ikke" goes in front of the finite verb "har".

gloss: …unless there are no more places available.
sentence: k:medmindre | n:der | a:ikke | v:er | N:flere ledige pladser
takeaway: "Medmindre" works like "hvis": subject ("der"), "ikke", then the verb.

gloss: …that many citizens can no longer afford the dentist.
sentence: k:at | n:mange borgere | a:ikke | a:længere | v:har | N:råd til tandlæge
takeaway: "Ikke længere" goes before "har" in an "at" clause, even in a long, formal sentence.

gloss: …because my employer has never paid out my holiday pay.
sentence: k:fordi | n:min arbejdsgiver | a:aldrig | v:har | V:udbetalt | N:mine feriepenge
takeaway: "Aldrig" goes before "har" after "fordi". The participle "udbetalt" follows the finite verb.

gloss: …if you really want to improve integration.
sentence: k:hvis | n:man | a:virkelig | v:vil | V:forbedre | N:integrationen
takeaway: "Virkelig" is a sentence adverb, so in a "hvis" clause it goes before "vil".

gloss: …even though it will probably cost more money in the short term.
sentence: k:selvom | n:det | a:formentlig | v:vil | V:koste | N:flere penge | A:på kort sigt
takeaway: "Formentlig" goes before the finite verb "vil", because "selvom" started a subordinate clause.

gloss: …since the politicians apparently have not listened to the experts.
sentence: k:da | n:politikerne | a:tilsyneladende | a:ikke | v:har | V:lyttet | A:til eksperterne
takeaway: Two sentence adverbs, "tilsyneladende ikke", and both come before "har".

gloss: …which the municipality has not been able to document.
sentence: k:som | n:kommunen | a:ikke | v:har | V:kunnet | V:dokumentere
takeaway: Relative clause, subordinate-clause order: "ikke" goes before "har", then "kunnet dokumentere".

gloss: …that my caseworker has never sent me.
sentence: k:som | n:min sagsbehandler | a:aldrig | v:har | V:sendt | N:mig
takeaway: "Aldrig" goes before "har" inside the relative clause, and "som" already stands for what was sent.

gloss: …that most citizens do not know at all.
sentence: k:som | n:de fleste borgere | a:slet ikke | v:kender
takeaway: "Slet ikke" goes before "kender", which is the ikke-rule inside a relative clause.

gloss: …where you can no longer get a doctor.
sentence: k:hvor | n:man | a:ikke | a:længere | v:kan | V:få | N:en læge
takeaway: "Hvor" opens the clause, and "ikke længere" goes before the finite verb "kan".

gloss: …that the government presented last week.
sentence: k:som | n:regeringen | v:fremlagde | A:i sidste uge
takeaway: After "som": the subject "regeringen", then the verb, then the time, with no inversion.

gloss: …where unfortunately the staff do not have time for the individual resident.
sentence: k:hvor | n:personalet | a:desværre | a:ikke | v:har | N:tid til den enkelte beboer
takeaway: "Desværre ikke" goes before "har", even in a long relative clause.

gloss: …that I have had at my current workplace since 2019.
sentence: k:som | n:jeg | v:har | V:haft | A:på min nuværende arbejdsplads | A:siden 2019
takeaway: Subordinate order after "som", and at the end place before time.

gloss: …that the municipality offers all newly arrived refugees.
sentence: k:som | n:kommunen | v:tilbyder | N:alle nyankomne flygtninge
takeaway: "Som" stands for the thing offered, so only the receiver is left in the object slot.

gloss: I would hereby like to give you an overview of the course of the case.
sentence: F:jeg | v:vil | a:hermed | V:give | N:Dem | N:et overblik over sagens forløb
alternatives: F:hermed | v:vil | n:jeg | V:give | N:Dem | N:et overblik over sagens forløb
takeaway: The formal "Dem" is the receiver and comes before the long direct object.

gloss: The municipality has ordered me to repay 12,000 kroner.
sentence: F:kommunen | v:har | V:pålagt | N:mig | N:en tilbagebetaling på 12.000 kroner
takeaway: "Pålægge nogen noget": the person comes first, then what is imposed.

gloss: The housing association has still not given us an explanation for the water damage.
sentence: F:boligselskabet | v:har | a:stadig | a:ikke | V:givet | N:os | N:en forklaring på vandskaden
takeaway: With "har … givet" the adverbs sit between the verbs, and "os" still comes before the thing given.

gloss: The employer should offer all employees a health check once a year.
sentence: F:arbejdsgiveren | v:bør | V:tilbyde | N:alle medarbejdere | N:et sundhedstjek | A:en gang om året
alternatives: F:en gang om året | v:bør | n:arbejdsgiveren | V:tilbyde | N:alle medarbejdere | N:et sundhedstjek
takeaway: "Alle medarbejdere" (receivers) comes before "et sundhedstjek" (what is offered), and the time comes last.

gloss: The school should have notified the parents of the change in good time.
sentence: F:skolen | v:burde | V:have | V:givet | N:forældrene | N:besked om ændringen | A:i god tid
alternatives: F:i god tid | v:burde | n:skolen | V:have | V:givet | N:forældrene | N:besked om ændringen
takeaway: "Give nogen besked": the receiver "forældrene" before "besked om ændringen".

gloss: My former employer refused me a reference.
sentence: F:min tidligere arbejdsgiver | v:nægtede | N:mig | N:en anbefaling
takeaway: "Nægte nogen noget" has the same order as "give": person, then thing.

gloss: The state should give the municipalities more funding for psychiatry.
sentence: F:staten | v:bør | V:give | N:kommunerne | N:flere midler til psykiatrien
takeaway: The receivers "kommunerne" come before "flere midler til psykiatrien", which is a typical opinion-text sentence.

gloss: The residents' association has written the mayor an open letter about the noise.
sentence: F:beboerforeningen | v:har | V:skrevet | N:borgmesteren | N:et åbent brev om støjen
takeaway: "Skrive nogen et brev": the receiver "borgmesteren" goes before the letter.

gloss: The municipality apparently has not dealt with my complaint yet.
sentence: F:kommunen | v:har | a:tilsyneladende | a:ikke | V:behandlet | N:min klage | A:endnu
alternatives: F:tilsyneladende | v:har | n:kommunen | a:ikke | V:behandlet | N:min klage | A:endnu
takeaway: "Tilsyneladende ikke" sits in the adverb slot between "har" and "behandlet". "Endnu" closes the sentence.

gloss: Many parents probably spend too much time on their mobile phones.
sentence: F:mange forældre | v:bruger | a:formentlig | N:for meget tid | A:på deres mobiltelefoner
alternatives: F:formentlig | v:bruger | n:mange forældre | N:for meget tid | A:på deres mobiltelefoner
takeaway: "Formentlig" comments on how sure the claim is, so it is a sentence adverb and sits right after the verb.

gloss: Under no circumstances can I accept this decision.
sentence: F:jeg | v:kan | a:under ingen omstændigheder | V:acceptere | N:denne afgørelse
alternatives: F:under ingen omstændigheder | v:kan | n:jeg | V:acceptere | N:denne afgørelse
takeaway: "Under ingen omstændigheder" is a negation, like "ikke", so it takes the central slot. You can also put it first.

gloss: I naturally have full understanding of your situation.
sentence: F:jeg | v:har | a:naturligvis | N:fuld forståelse for jeres situation
alternatives: F:naturligvis | v:har | n:jeg | N:fuld forståelse for jeres situation
takeaway: "Naturligvis" is a sentence adverb: after the verb, before the object.

gloss: Unfortunately many young people do not vote in the local elections.
sentence: F:mange unge | v:stemmer | a:desværre | a:ikke | A:ved kommunalvalget
alternatives: F:ved kommunalvalget | v:stemmer | n:mange unge | a:desværre | a:ikke
F:desværre | v:stemmer | n:mange unge | a:ikke | A:ved kommunalvalget
takeaway: "Desværre ikke" goes early, after the verb. "Ved kommunalvalget" is a content adverbial and comes last.

gloss: You should always read the contract carefully before signing it.
sentence: F:man | v:bør | a:altid | V:læse | N:kontrakten | A:grundigt | A:før underskrivelsen
alternatives: F:før underskrivelsen | v:bør | n:man | a:altid | V:læse | N:kontrakten | A:grundigt
takeaway: "Altid" is central and comes early. "Grundigt" (manner) and "før underskrivelsen" (time) come late.

gloss: I have not yet heard anything from Udbetaling Danmark.
sentence: F:jeg | v:har | a:endnu | a:ikke | V:hørt | N:noget | A:fra Udbetaling Danmark
alternatives: F:fra Udbetaling Danmark | v:har | n:jeg | a:endnu | a:ikke | V:hørt | N:noget
takeaway: "Endnu ikke" is in the adverb slot between "har" and "hørt". "Fra Udbetaling Danmark" goes at the end.

gloss: My son has cycled to school on his own since the summer holidays.
sentence: F:min søn | v:har | V:cyklet | A:alene | A:til skole | A:siden sommerferien
alternatives: F:siden sommerferien | v:har | n:min søn | V:cyklet | A:alene | A:til skole
takeaway: How ("alene"), where ("til skole"), since when ("siden sommerferien").

gloss: The staff work under enormous pressure on the ward during the holiday periods.
sentence: F:personalet | v:arbejder | A:under et enormt pres | A:på sengeafsnittet | A:i ferieperioderne
alternatives: F:på sengeafsnittet | v:arbejder | n:personalet | A:under et enormt pres | A:i ferieperioderne
F:i ferieperioderne | v:arbejder | n:personalet | A:under et enormt pres | A:på sengeafsnittet
takeaway: Even long adverbials follow manner, place, time: "under et enormt pres / på sengeafsnittet / i ferieperioderne".

gloss: We have been living temporarily with my mother-in-law since the water damage in March.
sentence: F:vi | v:har | V:boet | A:midlertidigt | A:hos min svigermor | A:siden vandskaden i marts
alternatives: F:hos min svigermor | v:har | n:vi | V:boet | A:midlertidigt | A:siden vandskaden i marts
F:siden vandskaden i marts | v:har | n:vi | V:boet | A:midlertidigt | A:hos min svigermor
takeaway: Manner, place, time: "midlertidigt hos min svigermor siden vandskaden i marts".

gloss: Citizens are treated differently in the country's municipalities.
sentence: F:borgerne | v:bliver | V:behandlet | A:forskelligt | A:i landets kommuner
alternatives: F:i landets kommuner | v:bliver | n:borgerne | V:behandlet | A:forskelligt
takeaway: Manner ("forskelligt") before place ("i landets kommuner").

gloss: I have worked as a volunteer at an asylum centre for over two years.
sentence: F:jeg | v:har | V:arbejdet | A:frivilligt | A:på et asylcenter | A:i over to år
alternatives: F:på et asylcenter | v:har | n:jeg | V:arbejdet | A:frivilligt | A:i over to år
F:i over to år | v:har | n:jeg | V:arbejdet | A:frivilligt | A:på et asylcenter
takeaway: Manner, place, then duration: "frivilligt på et asylcenter i over to år".

gloss: The ambulance arrived at the scene of the accident far too late last night.
sentence: F:ambulancen | v:ankom | A:alt for sent | A:til ulykkesstedet | A:i nat
alternatives: F:til ulykkesstedet | v:ankom | n:ambulancen | A:alt for sent | A:i nat
F:i nat | v:ankom | n:ambulancen | A:alt for sent | A:til ulykkesstedet
takeaway: "Alt for sent" (how), "til ulykkesstedet" (where), "i nat" (when).

gloss: Many commuters sit in queues on the motorway every morning.
sentence: F:mange pendlere | v:sidder | A:i kø | A:på motorvejen | A:hver morgen
alternatives: F:på motorvejen | v:sidder | n:mange pendlere | A:i kø | A:hver morgen
F:hver morgen | v:sidder | n:mange pendlere | A:i kø | A:på motorvejen
takeaway: Manner ("i kø"), then place ("på motorvejen"), then time ("hver morgen").

gloss: The doctor examined my daughter thoroughly at A&E last night.
sentence: F:lægen | v:undersøgte | N:min datter | A:grundigt | A:på skadestuen | A:i går aftes
alternatives: F:på skadestuen | v:undersøgte | n:lægen | N:min datter | A:grundigt | A:i går aftes
F:i går aftes | v:undersøgte | n:lægen | N:min datter | A:grundigt | A:på skadestuen
takeaway: After the object: manner ("grundigt"), place ("på skadestuen"), time ("i går aftes").

gloss: In future we must treat all citizens equally throughout the municipality.
sentence: F:vi | v:skal | V:behandle | N:alle borgere | A:ens | A:i hele kommunen | A:fremover
alternatives: F:i hele kommunen | v:skal | n:vi | V:behandle | N:alle borgere | A:ens | A:fremover
F:fremover | v:skal | n:vi | V:behandle | N:alle borgere | A:ens | A:i hele kommunen
takeaway: Manner ("ens"), place ("i hele kommunen"), time ("fremover").

gloss: (He says) that he is not coming to the party.
sentence: k:at | n:han | a:ikke | v:kommer | A:til festen
takeaway: After "Han siger" the at-clause is subordinate, so "ikke" goes before the verb: "at han ikke kommer", never "at han kommer ikke".

gloss: (She says) that she always works on Saturdays.
sentence: k:at | n:hun | a:altid | v:arbejder | A:om lørdagen
takeaway: Reported speech keeps subordinate order: "altid" sits before "arbejder", just as "ikke" would.

gloss: (They say) that they would be glad to help us.
sentence: k:at | n:de | a:gerne | v:vil | V:hjælpe | N:os
takeaway: Compare the main clause "De vil gerne hjælpe os" — after "at", "gerne" moves in front of the finite verb "vil".

gloss: (She writes) that she has not received the letter.
sentence: k:at | n:hun | a:ikke | v:har | V:modtaget | N:brevet
takeaway: In an at-clause "ikke" comes before the finite verb "har", and the participle "modtaget" still follows it.

gloss: (He tells me) that he has never been to Sweden.
sentence: k:at | n:han | a:aldrig | v:har | V:været | A:i Sverige
takeaway: Main clause: "Han har aldrig været i Sverige". Reported with "at": "at han aldrig har været" — the adverb jumps the finite verb.

gloss: (He explains) that his wife also wants to move to Aarhus.
sentence: k:at | n:hans kone | a:også | v:vil | V:flytte | A:til Aarhus
takeaway: "også" behaves exactly like "ikke": in the at-clause it stands between the subject and the finite verb "vil".

gloss: (The boss writes) that the meeting has unfortunately been cancelled.
sentence: k:at | n:mødet | a:desværre | v:er | V:blevet | V:aflyst
takeaway: "desværre" is a sentence adverb, so in reported speech it precedes the finite "er"; "blevet aflyst" waits in V.

gloss: (We tell the customer) that we probably cannot make it today.
sentence: k:at | n:vi | a:nok | a:ikke | v:kan | V:nå | N:det | A:i dag
takeaway: Two central adverbs, "nok ikke", travel together and both go before the finite verb "kan" in the at-clause.

gloss: (The tenant writes) that he can no longer pay the rent.
sentence: k:at | n:han | a:ikke | a:længere | v:kan | V:betale | N:huslejen
takeaway: "ikke længere" is a central adverbial pair; in the at-clause it lands before "kan" — "at han ikke længere kan betale".

gloss: (She writes) that she has not received an answer from the municipality either.
sentence: k:at | n:hun | a:heller ikke | v:har | V:fået | N:svar | A:fra kommunen
takeaway: Negated "også" is "heller ikke", and in an at-clause it comes before the finite verb "har", like "ikke" alone.

gloss: (She asks) whether we can come too.
sentence: k:om | n:vi | a:også | v:kan | V:komme
takeaway: A reported yes/no question opens with "om" (never "hvis"), and then has subordinate order: subject, adverb, finite verb.

gloss: (He asks) whether she still lives in Copenhagen.
sentence: k:om | n:hun | a:stadig | v:bor | A:i København
takeaway: The direct question is "Bor hun stadig i København?" — reported with "om", the subject comes first and "stadig" moves before "bor".

gloss: (Mum asks) whether the children have already eaten.
sentence: k:om | n:børnene | a:allerede | v:har | V:spist
takeaway: No inversion in a reported question: "om børnene allerede har spist", not "om har børnene spist".

gloss: (I ask) whether you would like to help me tomorrow.
sentence: k:om | n:du | a:gerne | v:vil | V:hjælpe | N:mig | A:i morgen
takeaway: "Vil du gerne hjælpe mig?" becomes "om du gerne vil hjælpe mig" — subject first, then "gerne", then the finite verb.

gloss: (She asks) whether I have ever been to Norway.
sentence: k:om | n:jeg | a:nogensinde | v:har | V:været | A:i Norge
takeaway: "nogensinde" is a central adverb, so after "om" it precedes the finite verb "har".

gloss: (I would like to know) whether the municipality also covers transport costs.
sentence: k:om | n:kommunen | a:også | v:dækker | N:udgifterne til transport
takeaway: In a formal enquiry the om-clause still follows the ledsætning schema: "om kommunen også dækker…", adverb before verb.

gloss: (I am writing to ask) whether we could possibly move the meeting to next week.
sentence: k:om | n:vi | a:muligvis | v:kan | V:flytte | N:mødet | A:til næste uge
takeaway: A polite request in an email is often an om-clause: "om vi muligvis kan flytte mødet" — "muligvis" before "kan".

gloss: (I would like to know) whether I am actually entitled to housing benefit.
sentence: k:om | n:jeg | a:faktisk | v:har | N:ret til boligstøtte
takeaway: "faktisk" is a sentence adverb: inside the om-clause it goes before the finite verb "har".

gloss: (She asks) why he did not come yesterday.
sentence: k:hvorfor | n:han | a:ikke | v:kom | A:i går
takeaway: Direct: "Hvorfor kom han ikke?" Reported: "hvorfor han ikke kom" — subject before the verb, "ikke" before the verb.

gloss: (Do you know) when the train actually leaves?
sentence: k:hvornår | n:toget | a:egentlig | v:kører
takeaway: A hv-word that opens a reported question works like "at" or "om": subject, then the adverb, then the verb.

gloss: (I wonder) where he always parks his car.
sentence: k:hvor | n:han | a:altid | v:parkerer | N:sin bil
takeaway: "Hvor parkerer han altid?" becomes "hvor han altid parkerer" once it is reported — no inversion, adverb first.

gloss: (I wonder) what she actually does at the weekend.
sentence: k:hvad | n:hun | a:egentlig | v:laver | A:i weekenden
takeaway: In the reported question "hvad" opens the clause and the subject follows straight after it: "hvad hun egentlig laver".

gloss: (I want to know) why you never answer my messages.
sentence: k:hvorfor | n:du | a:aldrig | v:svarer | A:på mine beskeder
takeaway: "aldrig" goes before "svarer" inside the hvorfor-clause, the mirror of the direct question "Hvorfor svarer du aldrig?".

gloss: (Tell me) what you do not understand.
sentence: k:hvad | n:du | a:ikke | v:forstår
takeaway: A reported hvad-question is a ledsætning: "hvad du ikke forstår", with "ikke" before the verb.

gloss: (The sign shows) where you may not smoke.
sentence: k:hvor | n:man | a:ikke | v:må | V:ryge
takeaway: After "hvor", "ikke" precedes the finite modal "må", and the infinitive "ryge" follows.

gloss: (I ask) when I can finally start the course.
sentence: k:hvornår | n:jeg | a:endelig | v:kan | V:begynde | A:på kurset
takeaway: "endelig" is a central adverb, so in the hvornår-clause it sits between "jeg" and "kan".

gloss: (Tell me) who is not coming to the meeting.
sentence: k:hvem | n:der | a:ikke | v:kommer | A:til mødet
takeaway: When the hv-word is itself the subject of a reported question, Danish adds "der" in the subject slot: "hvem der ikke kommer".

gloss: (I would like to know) why I have not yet received a reply to my application.
sentence: k:hvorfor | n:jeg | a:endnu | a:ikke | v:har | V:fået | N:svar | A:på min ansøgning
takeaway: A classic complaint-letter clause: "endnu ikke" before the finite "har", the participle "fået" after it.

gloss: (Please tell me) when the municipality is likely to reach a decision.
sentence: k:hvornår | n:kommunen | a:sandsynligvis | v:vil | V:træffe | N:en afgørelse
takeaway: "sandsynligvis" is a sentence adverb, so in the reported question it precedes the finite "vil".

gloss: When are you coming home?
sentence: F:hvornår | v:kommer | n:du | A:hjem
takeaway: The question word fills the Forfelt, so the verb comes second and the subject follows it: "Hvornår kommer du…?"

gloss: What are you doing this evening?
sentence: F:hvad | v:laver | n:du | A:i aften
takeaway: "Hvad" takes the front slot; the verb "laver" stays second and pushes "du" behind it.

gloss: Where does your brother live?
sentence: F:hvor | v:bor | n:din bror
takeaway: No "do" in Danish questions: the verb itself goes second, right after the question word.

gloss: Why don’t you eat fish?
sentence: F:hvorfor | v:spiser | n:du | a:ikke | N:fisk
takeaway: In a direct question the main-clause schema applies: verb second, then the subject, then "ikke".

gloss: When can we meet?
sentence: F:hvornår | v:kan | n:vi | V:mødes
takeaway: Only the finite "kan" is in slot 2; "mødes" waits at the end in V.

gloss: What have you not understood?
sentence: F:hvad | v:har | n:du | a:ikke | V:forstået
takeaway: A direct question keeps main-clause order: "har du ikke forstået". Compare the reported "hvad du ikke har forstået".

gloss: How long have you lived in Denmark?
sentence: F:hvor længe | v:har | n:du | V:boet | A:i Danmark
takeaway: "Hvor længe" is two words but one constituent — it fills the Forfelt alone, and "har" follows it.

gloss: Why have you never replied to my complaint?
sentence: F:hvorfor | v:har | n:I | a:aldrig | V:svaret | A:på min klage
takeaway: Main-clause question: "har I aldrig svaret" — the adverb follows the subject here, unlike in a reported question.

gloss: If it rains, we will stay at home.
sentence: F:hvis det regner | v:bliver | n:vi | A:hjemme
alternatives: F:vi | v:bliver | A:hjemme | A:hvis det regner
takeaway: A whole hvis-clause can fill the Forfelt. It counts as one constituent, so the verb comes next and the subject follows it: "bliver vi".

gloss: If I have time, I will call you.
sentence: F:hvis jeg har tid | v:ringer | n:jeg | A:til dig
alternatives: F:jeg | v:ringer | A:til dig | A:hvis jeg har tid
takeaway: Fronted hvis-clause, then verb, then subject: "Hvis jeg har tid, ringer jeg". Start with "jeg" and the clause goes to the end.

gloss: If you are ill, you should not go to work.
sentence: F:hvis du er syg | v:skal | n:du | a:ikke | V:gå | A:på arbejde
alternatives: F:du | v:skal | a:ikke | V:gå | A:på arbejde | A:hvis du er syg
takeaway: After the fronted hvis-clause the main clause is inverted — "skal du ikke gå" — with "ikke" after the subject, as in any main clause.

gloss: If the bus is delayed, I will be late.
sentence: F:hvis bussen er forsinket | v:kommer | n:jeg | A:for sent
alternatives: F:jeg | v:kommer | A:for sent | A:hvis bussen er forsinket
takeaway: However long the hvis-clause is, it is one Forfelt constituent — the next thing must be the verb "kommer".

gloss: If you have any questions, you are always welcome to contact me.
sentence: F:hvis du har spørgsmål | v:kan | n:du | a:altid | V:kontakte | N:mig
alternatives: F:du | v:kan | a:altid | V:kontakte | N:mig | A:hvis du har spørgsmål
takeaway: A standard email closing: "Hvis du har spørgsmål, kan du altid kontakte mig" — verb, subject, then "altid".

gloss: If I do not get an answer by Friday, I will send a complaint to the department.
sentence: F:hvis jeg ikke får svar inden fredag | v:vil | n:jeg | V:sende | N:en klage | A:til forvaltningen
alternatives: F:jeg | v:vil | V:sende | N:en klage | A:til forvaltningen | A:hvis jeg ikke får svar inden fredag
takeaway: Two rules in one sentence: "ikke" before "får" inside the hvis-clause, then inversion — "vil jeg" — once that clause is fronted.

gloss: (We are going to the beach) if it does not rain tomorrow.
sentence: k:hvis | n:det | a:ikke | v:regner | A:i morgen
takeaway: At the end of the sentence the hvis-clause has its own subordinate order: "hvis det ikke regner" — and the dummy subject "det" stays.

gloss: (Sign up by Friday) if you would like to take part.
sentence: k:hvis | n:I | a:gerne | v:vil | V:deltage
takeaway: "gerne" goes before the finite verb inside a hvis-clause: "hvis I gerne vil deltage".

gloss: (What do you do) if you never get an answer from the municipality?
sentence: k:hvis | n:man | a:aldrig | v:får | N:svar | A:fra kommunen
takeaway: "aldrig" sits before "får" in the hvis-clause — the same slot "ikke" would take.

gloss: Then we went home.
sentence: F:så | v:gik | n:vi | A:hjem
alternatives: F:vi | v:gik | a:så | A:hjem
takeaway: Fronted "så" (then) is an ordinary adverb in the Forfelt, so the verb comes second: "Så gik vi", never "Så vi gik".

gloss: Then we eat dinner.
sentence: F:så | v:spiser | n:vi | N:aftensmad
alternatives: F:vi | v:spiser | a:så | N:aftensmad
takeaway: Starting with "så" triggers inversion just like "i dag" or "derfor": verb, then subject.

gloss: Then I can’t come.
sentence: F:så | v:kan | n:jeg | a:ikke | V:komme
alternatives: F:jeg | v:kan | a:så | a:ikke | V:komme
takeaway: "Så" in front means "in that case": the verb "kan" stays second, the subject follows, then "ikke".

gloss: Then she took the bus into town.
sentence: F:så | v:tog | n:hun | N:bussen | A:ind til byen
alternatives: F:hun | v:tog | a:så | N:bussen | A:ind til byen
takeaway: Telling a story in steps? Each fronted "så" pushes the subject behind the verb: "Så tog hun bussen".

gloss: Then we will have to wait until tomorrow.
sentence: F:så | v:må | n:vi | V:vente | A:til i morgen
alternatives: F:vi | v:må | a:så | V:vente | A:til i morgen
takeaway: Fronted "så" takes the Forfelt; "må" stays in slot 2 and "vi" follows it.

gloss: So I stayed at home all week.
sentence: F:så | v:blev | n:jeg | A:hjemme | A:hele ugen
alternatives: F:jeg | v:blev | a:så | A:hjemme | A:hele ugen
takeaway: As a new sentence, "Så" (so, therefore) is fronted and inverts: "Så blev jeg hjemme" — then place before time.

gloss: (I write it down) so that I don’t forget it.
sentence: k:så | n:jeg | a:ikke | v:glemmer | N:det
takeaway: "Så" meaning "so that" opens a subordinate clause, so "ikke" comes before the verb: "så jeg ikke glemmer det".

gloss: (Let’s leave now) so that we are not late.
sentence: k:så | n:vi | a:ikke | v:kommer | A:for sent
takeaway: A purpose clause with "så": subject, "ikke", then the verb — the ledsætning schema, not the main-clause one.

gloss: (We have extended our opening hours) so that customers can always get in touch with us.
sentence: k:så | n:kunderne | a:altid | v:kan | V:komme | A:i kontakt med os
takeaway: In a "so that" clause "altid" goes before the finite "kan", exactly as "ikke" would.

gloss: (Remember to register in time) so that you do not lose your right to unemployment benefit.
sentence: k:så | n:De | a:ikke | v:mister | N:Deres ret til dagpenge
takeaway: Purpose "så" is subordinate: "så De ikke mister…". Main-clause order here would read as "so (as a result) you don’t lose".

gloss: She is not coming today because she is ill.
sentence: F:hun | v:kommer | a:ikke | A:i dag | A:fordi hun er syg
alternatives: F:fordi hun er syg | v:kommer | n:hun | a:ikke | A:i dag
F:i dag | v:kommer | n:hun | a:ikke | A:fordi hun er syg
takeaway: The fordi-clause is one content adverbial: it goes at the end, or in the Forfelt — and then the main clause inverts.

gloss: I always call my mother when I am ill.
sentence: F:jeg | v:ringer | a:altid | A:til min mor | A:når jeg er syg
alternatives: F:når jeg er syg | v:ringer | n:jeg | a:altid | A:til min mor
takeaway: "altid" belongs in the central slot of the main clause; the når-clause is a content adverbial at the end — or fronted, with inversion.

gloss: He always says that he is busy.
sentence: F:han | v:siger | a:altid | N:at han har travlt
takeaway: The at-clause is the object of "siger" and comes last; the main clause’s own "altid" stays right after the verb.

gloss: I would like to know whether I can take leave.
sentence: F:jeg | v:vil | a:gerne | V:vide | N:om jeg kan få orlov
takeaway: "Jeg vil gerne vide" is an ordinary main clause; the om-clause is simply its object, placed in N.

gloss: She also asked the teacher when the course starts.
sentence: F:hun | v:spurgte | a:også | N:læreren | N:hvornår kurset begynder
takeaway: Two objects: the person asked ("læreren") first, then the reported question. "også" stays in the central slot.

gloss: When the neighbours have a party, I can never sleep.
sentence: F:når naboerne fester | v:kan | n:jeg | a:aldrig | V:sove
alternatives: F:jeg | v:kan | a:aldrig | V:sove | A:når naboerne fester
takeaway: A fronted når-clause fills the Forfelt, so "kan" comes next, then "jeg", then "aldrig" — main-clause order.

gloss: Although I have written several times, the municipality still has not replied.
sentence: F:selvom jeg har skrevet flere gange | v:har | n:kommunen | a:stadig | a:ikke | V:svaret
alternatives: F:kommunen | v:har | a:stadig | a:ikke | V:svaret | A:selvom jeg har skrevet flere gange
takeaway: A fronted selvom-clause is one constituent; the main clause then inverts: "har kommunen stadig ikke svaret".

gloss: I do not think that the proposal solves the problem.
sentence: F:jeg | v:mener | a:ikke | N:at forslaget løser problemet
takeaway: In an opinion text the negation belongs to "mener": "Jeg mener ikke, at…" — "ikke" after the main verb, the at-clause last.
